compiled_state.description:
# live_jira_dc harness exhausts Jira DC's 10-PAT-per-user cap

## Context / Problem

The live Jira DC harness tier dies at SETUP, so no live acceptance evidence can be produced at
all — and every remaining story in epic e369 (notably J11, the epic's headline live proof) runs
on this harness. Reproduced across two independent CI runs (30604756524, 30623000498), same
signature:

    ERROR at setup of test_add_label_and_the_links_surface_against_a_real_instance
    AssertionError: PAT creation failed: 403
      {'exception': 'com.atlassian.pats.exception.UserTokenLimitExceededException',
       'error': "You can't create more than 10 tokens."}

`jira_dc_pat` (`tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py:355`) is declared `@pytest.fixture` with
NO scope, so it is FUNCTION-scoped: every test that requests it mints a brand new Personal
Access Token via `POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens` and never deletes it. Jira Data Center caps a
user at 10 PATs. Consumption therefore grows as O(tests) while the budget is fixed at 10.

Two properties make this expensive to diagnose, and both are reasons to fix it properly rather
than by trimming test count:

* **It mis-attributes.** The ERROR surfaces at setup of a test in `test_transport.py` — a module
  nobody touched — because that is merely the test that happened to run once the budget was
  spent. The cause is session-wide.
* **It looks flaky but is deterministic.** The fixture mints with `expirationDuration=1`, so
  tokens self-clear after a day. Whether a run fails depends on how recently the instance was
  used, not on chance.

## Approach

**Make `jira_dc_pat` SESSION-scoped**, turning PAT consumption from O(tests) into O(1).

This is the fix that scales, and scaling is the actual requirement: J11 adds substantially more
live tests to this tier, so any fix whose budget is still proportional to test count merely
moves the cliff. Every consumer needs only *a* valid PAT — no test in this tier asserts
per-token behaviour (verified: the fixture's only assertions are on `rawToken`, and its sole
consumers use it as a bearer credential) — so one token per run is behaviourally identical to
one per test.

**Rejected: per-test teardown via `DELETE /rest/pat/latest/tokens/{id}`.** It preserves
per-test isolation that nothing here needs, costs an API call per test, and — decisively — it
is not verified to be implementable: the creation response is only asserted to carry
`rawToken`, and whether it also returns an `id` has NOT been confirmed against a live instance.
Choosing it would make the fix depend on an unverified response field. Session scope depends on
nothing new.

**Complementary: sweep leftover `rebar-j5-harness-*` tokens at session start**, mirroring
`_leaked_scratch_projects()` (`conftest.py:181`), which already does exactly this for scratch
PROJECTS left by interrupted runs. Session scope alone fixes consumption WITHIN a run; it does
not help a run that starts against an instance already holding 10 tokens from a crashed
predecessor. Both layers are required for the ACs below, and they address different failures.

The sweep uses the same defensive posture the project fixture already establishes: read the
token list from its direct REST endpoint and, if it cannot be enumerated, **return empty rather
than invent a failure** — a sweep that cannot see is not evidence of cleanliness, and the
harness-readiness assertion remains authoritative for usability. Deleting a leftover token is
likewise best-effort: a failed delete is reported, not fatal, because the session-scoped mint
that follows is the real test of whether headroom exists.

**Raw `urllib` REST is correct here and is not a divergence from "never hand-roll REST".** That
rule governs the DC *transport*, which must go through `pycontribs/jira`. This conftest
deliberately speaks raw REST v2 with stdlib `urllib` only (see its module docstring) so the
harness does not depend on the client library the harness exists to validate. The sweep reuses
the existing `_request` helper.

## Scope

- `tests/external/live_jira_dc/conftest.py` — change `jira_dc_pat` to `scope="session"`,
  document the 10-token cap in its docstring, and add a `_leaked_harness_tokens()` helper plus
  its invocation from the existing session-scoped `_jira_dc_harness_ready` autouse fixture.
- `tests/unit/` — unit coverage for the sweep helper's parsing and its
  cannot-enumerate/failed-delete degradation, exercised against a stubbed `_request` so it runs
  in the normal (non-live) tier.

No production `src/rebar` code changes: this is a test-harness defect.

## Testing

The live tier cannot run on this workstation (its base image is linux/amd64 only and this is
Apple Silicon — `tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md:54-73`), so the split is deliberate:

* **Unit (runs everywhere, in CI on every change):** the sweep helper returns the leftover
  token names/ids from a well-formed list response; returns EMPTY when the endpoint errors or
  returns a non-list (the cannot-enumerate path); ignores tokens not carrying the
  `rebar-j5-harness-` prefix (so it never deletes a human's unrelated PAT — the failure mode
  that would make this fix worse than the bug); and does not raise when a DELETE fails.
* **Live (GitHub Actions `jira DC harness smoke` job):** the acceptance evidence. The full
  `tests/external/live_jira_dc` suite completes with no `UserTokenLimitExceededException`.
  Because session scope makes consumption O(1), one token is consumed regardless of test count,
  which is what supplies headroom rather than a coincidence of the current count.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `jira_dc_pat` is `scope="session"`, verified by reading the fixture declaration, so a run
      mints exactly ONE PAT no matter how many tests request it
- [ ] the full `tests/external/live_jira_dc` suite runs in the GitHub Actions
      `jira DC harness smoke` job with ZERO `UserTokenLimitExceededException`, confirmed by
      reading that job's log — not the overall run status
- [ ] headroom is structural, not coincidental: because consumption is O(1) in test count, the
      run above passes with MORE live tests present than the count that first triggered the cap
- [ ] a leftover `rebar-j5-harness-*` token from a crashed run is deleted at session start, so
      it does not break the next run — covered by a unit test against a stubbed `_request`
- [ ] the sweep never deletes a token lacking the `rebar-j5-harness-` prefix, asserted by unit
      test
- [ ] the sweep degrades safely: a non-200/non-list list response yields an empty result rather
      than an exception, and a failed DELETE does not abort the session — both unit-tested
- [ ] the 10-token cap and the session-scope decision are documented in the `jira_dc_pat`
      docstring, since the cap is a non-obvious Jira DC limit
